title: Token Pace Validation Harness & p95 Drift Watcher for Core Models
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a reproducible token-per-second microbenchmark harness (Token Pace Validation Harness) targeted at our core production models. The harness must: 1) produce stable, repeatable TPS numbers, 2) track p95/p99 latency regressions, 3) surface root-cause signals (KV cache warm ratio, batch size distribution, GPU stall counters), and 4) integrate with CI, Grafana dashboards, and alerting for regression detection.

Background: Current throughput regressions are often discovered late in canaries or customer incidents. We need a lightweight, fast-running suite that runs nightly and as a pre-merge optional job for infra/model changes to catch regressions earlier. Existing microbench assets are large and focus on long sustained runs; this ticket scopes a compact harness optimized for quick feedback while still capturing meaningful p95 trends.

Non-goals: Full long-duration soak tests (covered by separate suites), end-to-end customer workload replay, and synthetic text-quality evaluation.

Success criteria (high level): Harness runs in < 20 minutes for core set, produces TPS and p95 baselines within ±3% across repeated runs on the same infra, and triggers a CI alert or PagerDuty when regression thresholds are crossed.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A runnable benchmark binary + config stored in repo that executes the core matrix in <= 20 minutes.
2) Outputs JSON artifacts with metrics: tokens_per_sec, p50, p95, p99, gpu_util_pct, kv_cache_warm_pct, batch_size_histogram.
3) Nightly CI job scheduled; artifacts pushed to S3/GCS and parsed into the Perf/TokenPace Grafana dashboard.
4) Regression rule: fail if tokens_per_sec drops >= 10% vs baseline OR p95 increases >= 20% vs baseline; detect and create a Linear regression alert.
5) A short runbook describing reproducing steps and common mitigations merged to Confluence.
proposed_approach:
Implement a compact harness in the perf-harness repo using the existing runtime client. Key elements: deterministic prompt templates, KV cache warm-up sequences, progressive concurrency sweep (1,2,4,8 workers), and per-run garbage collection of caches. Add a small state store for baselines (S3/GCS json blobs) and a comparator that emits a regression artifact. Hook results into an existing Lambda that writes metrics to Prometheus/Grafana and ties into PagerDuty for severe regressions.

Implementation phases: Phase 1 - MVP harness + single-model run. Phase 2 - extend to core matrix and CI integration. Phase 3 - dashboarding, alert tuning, and canary gating.
test_matrix: Models: rwkv-13b, redwood-7b-instruct, open-13b-quant (approx names). Sequence lengths: 64, 256, 1024. Token outputs: 32, 128. Concurrency sweep: 1,2,4,8 workers. KV-warm modes: cold start, warm prefix (200 tokens). Hardware targets: g4dn-equivalent (dev), p4-equivalent (perf). Metrics to collect: tokens_per_sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, gpu_util_pct, memory_alloc_mb, kv_cache_warm_pct, batch_size_histogram, kernel_stalls.
integration: CI: nightly workflow in .github/workflows/perf-token-pace.yml and optional pre-merge job. Observability: Perf/TokenPace Grafana dashboard (panel links in artifacts). Alerts: PagerDuty via Alertmanager for P0 regressions and Slack #perf-alerts for P1. Artifact storage: gs://redwood-perf/token-pace/ (JSON run artifacts).
